title: Tamsin and the Vow
premise: Ansel Okafor, a wedding planner whose own engagement ended in a scandal she never explains, agrees to pose as the girlfriend of her estranged childhood friend Tamsin Adeyemi for one weekend — Tamsin's family reunion, where a decade-old vow made on their grandmother's deathbed is about to be called in. The vow: that Tamsin would marry before her thirtieth birthday or forfeit her inheritance of the family's beloved lakeside inn. But the fake romance turns real by dessert, and Ansel discovers the vow was never about marriage at all — it was grandmother's coded way of forcing Tamsin to reconcile with the sister she betrayed. As the birthday deadline looms and Ansel's past collides with Tamsin's family in devastating ways, both women must choose between keeping a promise and telling the truth. In the end, the vow is broken openly, the inn is saved through honesty instead of obligation, and Ansel says the sentence she rehearsed for ten years — not 'I do,' but 'I forgive myself' — as she and Tamsin begin something real.
about_author: Jude Fairweather is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent seven years watching other people's love stories from behind the cake table before writing her own. She lives near a lake she refuses to name, where she writes romances about people who are terrible at saying what they mean.

chapters.title: The Last Wedding
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She flawlessly executes her two-hundredth wedding while privately dismantling her belief in them, then finds an unopened letter from Tamsin Adeyemi in her mail. Beat: competent numbness cracked open by the past.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Flashback woven through present: the friendship with Tamsin that ended the night Ansel's engagement collapsed and she left town without explanation. She rereads the letter three times. Beat: guilt resurfacing like a bruise.

chapters.title: The Letter's Terms
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. We learn why she wrote: the family reunion, the inheritance clause, and her desperation. She offers Ansel money for one weekend as her girlfriend. Beat: pride wrestling with panic.

chapters.title: A Price for Pretending
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel arrives at the crumbling-but-beautiful Lakeside Inn to negotiate terms and is ambushed by Tamsin's enormous, warm, chaotic family. Beat: fish-out-of-water comedy masking old wounds.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Over wine on the dock, they draft fake-relationship rules: no real feelings, no questions about the past, leave Sunday night. Both break rule three within the hour. Beat: banter sharpening into intimacy.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Room
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Tamsin shows her the sealed room kept as Grandma Ruthie left it, including the framed vow document. Ansel notices something odd in its wording. Beat: mystery seeded beneath nostalgia.

chapters.title: Dinner with the Adeyemis
chapters.summary: Ensemble scene, mostly Ansel's POV. The first family dinner: probing questions, Tamsin's hand finding hers under the table, and a pointed toast from Aunt Bisi about 'promises kept.' Beat: performance becoming second nature.

chapters.title: By Dessert
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. During dessert, Tamsin catches herself believing the fiction — laughing at Ansel's jokes, memorizing her face. She retreats to the kitchen and is followed. A near-kiss interrupted by Cousin Dele. Beat: the fake tipping toward real.

chapters.title: Sunday Refusal
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Sunday comes; neither mentions her leaving. She stays another night 'to help with inventory,' lying to herself about why. Beat: quiet surrender to wanting.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Left
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. We meet Ngozi, Tamsin's older sister, who arrives late and unwelcome — the family rift revealed. Tamsin's coldness unsettles Ansel, who recognizes avoidance when she sees it. Beat: the vow's true shape begins to emerge.

chapters.title: Inventory and Confessions
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Counting linens at midnight, Tamsin almost tells Ansel what happened with Ngozi; instead she asks about Ansel's broken engagement. Ansel deflects with a joke that doesn't land. Beat: intimacy blocked by symmetry of secrets.

chapters.title: The Lawyer's Call
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The estate lawyer confirms: the vow executes on Tamsin's thirtieth birthday, six weeks away. Marriage or the inn passes to a development consortium. Panic hardens into scheming. Beat: ticking clock installed.

chapters.title: An Extension of the Lie
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel proposes staying through the birthday — a real engagement announcement, a real wedding if it comes to that. Tamsin, horrified and thrilled, accepts. Beat: the lie escalating beyond control.

chapters.title: Meeting the Mother
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Mama Adeyemi takes Ansel to the market, dissects her intentions with terrifying gentleness, and reveals she knows the relationship began suspiciously recently. Beat: maternal scrutiny as rising threat.

chapters.title: What Ngozi Knows
chapters.summary: Ngozi's POV. Ngozi recognizes Ansel from a decade ago — she was there the night everything fell apart at Ansel's rehearsal dinner. She says nothing yet, but starts asking questions. Beat: the past acquiring a witness.

chapters.title: Rehearsing the Vow
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin practices her grandmother's vow aloud and finally reads its full text: it requires not just marriage but 'a household built on truth.' She dismisses the phrase as sentimentality. Beat: dramatic irony tightening.

chapters.title: Storm on the Lake
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Caught in a squall while securing the docks, Ansel and Tamsin shelter in the boathouse and kiss properly for the first time. Afterward, Tamsin whispers 'this isn't pretend anymore' — and immediately regrets saying it. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Retreat
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Terrified of wanting more than the deadline allows, Tamsin reverts to business: wedding planning spreadsheets, guest lists, a venue tour. Ansel plays along, wounded. Beat: love weaponized into logistics.

chapters.title: The Ex Arrives
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Marcus, Ansel's former fiancé, appears at the inn — invited by Ngozi, who has been digging. His presence forces Ansel to perform happiness while he drops loaded references to 'that night.' Beat: external pressure mounting.

chapters.title: That Night, Part One
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Partial flashback: the rehearsal dinner, the fight, the thing Ansel said that ended her engagement and her friendship with Tamsin simultaneously. The chapter cuts off before the revelation. Beat: withheld truth as engine.

chapters.title: That Night, Part Two
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The full truth: Ansel discovered Marcus's infidelity, and Tamsin — who knew and stayed silent to protect the group — let her walk down the aisle toward humiliation. Ansel fled rather than confront either betrayal. Beat: sympathy redistributed; both women were cowards.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Dock
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating. Ansel finally tells Tamsin why she vanished; Tamsin admits she knew about Marcus. Ten years of silence explained in one brutal, cathartic argument. Beat: the central wound opened at last.

chapters.title: Cold Beds, Warm Kitchen
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Days of frosty coexistence; the family senses the fracture. Then Mama Adeyemi falls ill briefly, and the two women keep vigil together, speaking again in small mercies. Beat: reconciliation beginning through shared care.

chapters.title: Ngozi's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Ngozi's POV. Ngozi confronts Tamsin privately: tell the family the truth about the vow's origin, or she will. She reveals Grandma Ruthie wrote the vow after Ngozi's exile — as a lever, not a punishment. Beat: the mystery's key turns.

chapters.title: The Vow's Origin
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Flashback to Grandma Ruthie's deathbed: the vow wasn't about marriage at all. It was designed to force Tamsin to bring Ngozi home — 'a household built on truth' meant reconciling the sisters. Tamsin has been solving the wrong problem. Beat: devastating reframing.

chapters.title: Why Ngozi Left
chapters.summary: Ngozi's POV. Ngozi's side: she took the fall for a financial disaster Tamsin caused at nineteen, was exiled by the family, and never corrected the record out of loyalty. Loyalty versus truth, embodied. Beat: theme crystallized in backstory.

chapters.title: The Consortium's Offer
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The developers make a direct play: cash now, no wedding required, plus a job offer for Ansel in the city. Ansel realizes she wants the inn, not the escape. Beat: temptation refused, desire clarified.

chapters.title: Planning a Real Wedding
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. With three weeks left, Ansel plans the wedding she once swore off — and finds joy in it, because this time it's honest. Tamsin watches her work and falls harder. Beat: vocation and love reunited.

chapters.title: Mama Knows
chapters.summary: Mama Adeyemi's POV. Mama reveals she has known the relationship started as a arrangement since week one — and that she let it continue because she watched it become true. She asks only for truth before the birthday. Beat: parental blessing earned through honesty.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal Dinner
chapters.summary: Ensemble, Ansel's POV. A mirror of the disastrous dinner ten years ago: same family, same table, Marcus gone, Ngozi invited. Old ghosts surface when a cousin toasts 'the Adeyemi talent for forgiveness.' Beat: history rhyming, tension peaking.

chapters.title: Ngozi Tells the Truth
chapters.summary: Ngozi's POV. At the dinner's end, Ngozi publicly confesses the cover-up of the nineteen-year-old disaster — exposing Tamsin's old fault and her own decade of silent loyalty. The family erupts. Beat: truth detonating the inheritance plot.

chapters.title: The Family Fractures
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Accusations fly; Aunt Bisi demands the inn be sold anyway; Mama wavers. Tamsin, blamed anew, nearly signs the consortium papers at midnight. Beat: darkest hour.

chapters.title: Ansel's Sentence
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel stands before the family and delivers the sentence rehearsed for a decade: a full account of her own flight, cowardice, and the cost of silence — modeling the vulnerability everyone else is avoiding. Beat: climax of character; the theme spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Breaking the Vow
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. On her birthday, before lawyer and family, Tamsin formally declines to fulfill the vow — declaring that Ruthie's real wish was truth, not a wedding, and that the inn will stand on honesty or not at all. She tears the document. Beat: climax of plot.

chapters.title: What the Will Actually Said
chapters.summary: Lawyer's letter, read in Tamsin's POV. A codicil surfaces: if the vow was refused 'for reasons of truth,' the inn passes to both sisters jointly. Ruthie planned for courage all along. Beat: reversal rewarding integrity.

chapters.title: Sisters at the Dock
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Tamsin and Ngozi rebuild, awkwardly, over repairs to the boathouse storm damage. Not forgiven instantly — but begun. Beat: found-and-recovered family.

chapters.title: No More Past Tense
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel, offered a dream job in the city, chooses the inn and a life with Tamsin — proposed to, this time, with no deadline attached. Tamsin says yes on no schedule at all. Beat: love chosen freely, not contractually.

chapters.title: The Wedding That Wasn't Owed
chapters.summary: Ensemble, Ansel's POV. They marry a year later at the inn — small, imperfect, joyful. Ansel plans every detail and cries through all of them. Ngozi is maid of honor; Mama officiates. Beat: full-circle celebration.

chapters.title: Grandma Ruthie's Room, Opened
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The sealed room is finally reopened and turned into a family archive. Among Ruthie's papers, a note: 'If they choose truth, I win either way.' Beat: thematic seal; the dead grandmother's blessing.

chapters.title: Vow Renewed
chapters.summary: Alternating final POVs. One year on: the inn thrives, the sisters run it together, Ansel plans weddings she believes in again. On the dock at dusk, the two women write new vows — private ones, with no deadline, no witnesses, no conditions. Beat: peace earned; the story closed on chosen love.
